high.title: Vamos (VAMO3) leads Ibovespa gains and BRAV3 is worst performing stock; see weekly highlights
high.summary: The Ibovespa broke its streak of weekly gains despite renewing historical highs and geopolitical tensions easing, falling 0.81% to close at 195,733.51 points. The main culprit was oil prices returning to $90 levels. However, the index set new records during the week, reaching 198,657.33 points on Tuesday and hitting an intraday high of 199,354.81 points - a new nominal historical maximum. The USD/BRL pair closed at R$ 4.9833, at its lowest level since mid-2024, with the real strengthening 0.56% against the dollar over five trading sessions. This represents significant BRL strength that FX traders should monitor closely. The market continued focusing on Middle East conflict effects and monetary policy implications, while electoral polls also remained on the radar. The combination of near-record Ibovespa levels and BRL strength suggests continued foreign capital inflows, but oil price volatility poses risks to the sustainability of these moves.

medium.title: Vale (VALE3): is it time to invest? Analyst gives 5 reasons to buy shares; check recommendation
medium.summary: Vale (VALE3) underperformed in March with a 6% decline versus Ibovespa's 0.9% drop, closing at R$ 82.48. However, Empiricus Research analyst Ruy Hungria considers this decline "unjustified" and believes the shares can continue "unlocking value." By Wednesday's close, Vale had recovered to R$ 88.44, fully recovering March losses and supporting the investment thesis. The analyst maintains his buy recommendation based on five key factors, suggesting the mining giant remains attractive despite broader market volatility affecting commodity stocks.

medium.title: Top picks: PRIO3, ROXO34, VALE3 and more stocks to invest with Ibovespa near 200,000 points, according to Empiricus
medium.summary: Foreign investors continue injecting capital into Brazilian stocks despite Middle East geopolitical tensions, with approximately R$ 70 billion in foreign inflows helping drive Ibovespa's 22.1% gain in 2026. April alone saw over R$ 14 billion in foreign investment by April 14th, pushing the index above 198,000 points to new historical highs. Empiricus Research believes profit opportunities remain despite elevated valuations, but emphasizes the need for "high selectivity" in stock picking as the market is no longer a broad bargain.
